question: Lion Holdings Pte Ltd owns 90% of the ordinary shares of Merlion Trading Pte Ltd, and Merlion Trading owns 80% of Merlion Logistics Pte Ltd. All three are Singapore-incorporated with December year ends. Can Merlion Logistics transfer its current-year trade loss to Lion Holdings under group relief?

Orchid Pte Ltd holds 500,000 of the 1,000,000 plain shares in Lotus Pte Ltd and all 1,000,000 of Lotus's preference shares. The preference shares pay a fixed 6% dividend and also share in whatever profit is left after that dividend. For the 75% group relief shareholding test, do the preference shares count?

Harbour Holdings Pte Ltd acquired 100% of Bayfront Pte Ltd on 1 July 2024; its other subsidiary, Quayside Pte Ltd, has been wholly owned for years. All three have 31 December year ends. For YA 2025 Bayfront has a $400,000 unabsorbed trade loss and Quayside has assessable income of $1,000,000. How much of the loss can Quayside claim?
Pearl Engineering Pte Ltd's branch in Ho Chi Minh City made a loss of S$250,000 in FY2024. Can Pearl hand that branch loss to its profitable sister company in the same wholly owned Singapore group?

Jade Biotech Pte Ltd enjoys pioneer status under the EEIA, and its pioneer activity made a loss this year. Can the loss be passed to a profitable sister company under group relief, and does that change once the pioneer period ends?

Our client was granted an investment allowance under the EEIA for its new automation line, but its income this year is too small to absorb it. Can the unused allowance be transferred to a profitable group company?

Granite Investments Pte Ltd only holds rental properties, and its income is computed under the special rules for companies whose business is making investments. For YA 2025 its property outgoings exceed its rental income, and it also has cash donations made in 2024 that it cannot use. Which of these can it pass to a profitable group company?

For YA 2025 Cedar Pte Ltd has an adjusted trade profit of $200,000, capital allowances brought forward of $50,000, current-year capital allowances of $120,000 and trade losses brought forward of $90,000. It would like to absorb the old trade losses first so that its current-year allowances can be passed to a sister company. Is that allowed, and what can it transfer?

Birch Pte Ltd's income taxed at the normal corporate rate is $180,000 before it claims $150,000 of a sister company's current-year losses. Is its partial tax exemption worked out on $180,000 or on $30,000?

Teak Pte Ltd has $500,000 of current-year trade losses to give away and has named Oak Pte Ltd as its first claimant and Pine Pte Ltd as its second. Oak has $300,000 of available assessable income and Pine has $400,000. The directors want to split the losses equally, $250,000 each. Can they?

Ash Pte Ltd's Form GR A lists Fir Pte Ltd before Yew Pte Ltd, while Elm Pte Ltd's lists Yew before Fir. On the claimant side, Fir's Form GR B wants Elm's losses first and Yew's wants Ash's first, so the priorities cannot all be honoured. Whose ordering wins?
Willow Pte Ltd usually files the simplified Form C-S. For YA 2025 it wants to absorb its sister company's current-year loss under group relief. Can it keep filing Form C-S?

After the group's YA 2024 returns were filed, IRAS finalised the transferor's assessment and its allowable loss went up by $60,000. Do the transferor and the claimants now have to lodge fresh group relief forms for the extra amount?

Spruce Pte Ltd's Form GR A for YA 2024 named Maple Pte Ltd and then Cherry Pte Ltd as claimants. Hazel Pte Ltd, a group company that filed a loss return, has just received a notice of assessment showing assessable income instead. Can Spruce now put Hazel ahead of Maple?

Redwood Pte Ltd is buying all the shares of Sequoia Pte Ltd, which expects large losses on contracts it already holds but has not yet booked them. Redwood plans to absorb those losses under group relief once Sequoia books them after completion. What is the tax risk?

Newco Pte Ltd was incorporated on 1 March 2024 as a wholly owned subsidiary and made up its first accounts to 30 June 2025 to match the group's June year end. The 16-month period shows a loss. How should the loss be dealt with for group relief, and for which YAs?

Banyan Pte Ltd has accumulated losses and negative net assets, so the notional $100 of residual assets is used for the group relief entitlement test. Its parent holds all of Banyan's ordinary shares, valued at $600, and an outside lender has a $400 loan whose return rises and falls with Banyan's profits. The parent and the lender have made no special arrangement on how assets would be shared. How is the parent's share of the $100 worked out, and does it reach 75%?

Cypress Holdings Pte Ltd closes its books on 31 March, but its two wholly owned Singapore subsidiaries both have 31 December year ends. The holding company is neither giving nor receiving any losses. Can one subsidiary transfer its current-year loss to the other?

Fig Pte Ltd has YA 2025 assessable income of $600,000 and has already absorbed $250,000 of losses from its first-priority transferor. All the companies were in the group for the whole year and share a December year end. Under s 37B(10), how much of Fig's income is left for losses from its second transferor?

Mango Pte Ltd's YA 2025 income after capital allowances and losses is $900,000, and it also has an EEIA investment allowance of $300,000 for the year. Under the s 37B(19) definition, is its assessable income for capping the group relief it can claim $900,000 or $600,000?

Kiwi Pte Ltd transfers $170,000 of current-year unabsorbed capital allowances, all relating to its income taxed at a 10% concessionary rate, to Papaya Pte Ltd, whose $500,000 of chargeable income is all taxed at 17%. Applying s 37B(17), by how much is Papaya's chargeable income reduced?

A Singapore group contains two life insurers. Under s 37B(15A), can the first insurer pass to the second a qualifying deduction attached to the part of its participating-fund income allocated to policyholders?
Two years after Plum Pte Ltd claimed $400,000 of losses from a sister company, IRAS finds that the sister's loss had been overstated by $150,000. What can the Comptroller do under s 37B(16)?

Pinnacle Pte Ltd holds 80% of Summit Pte Ltd's ordinary shares, but because an unrelated party has lent Summit money on profit-sharing terms, Pinnacle is entitled to only 70% of Summit's residual profits. Does Pinnacle meet s 37B(4), so that the two are in the same group?
Under Malaysia's group relief rules, what percentage of a company's current-year adjusted loss can it surrender to a related Malaysian company?
Can our client's Singapore subsidiaries register as a single GST group so that the management fees they charge each other are disregarded for GST?
Is stamp duty relief available under the Stamp Duties Act when a parent transfers a warehouse to its 90%-owned subsidiary as part of an internal restructuring?
Under the Companies Act, can a subsidiary in a small group be exempted from having its financial statements audited?
Can an Australian head company and its wholly owned Australian subsidiaries elect to be taxed as a single consolidated group?
Within how many days after its AGM must a company lodge its annual return with ACRA?
Delta Pte Ltd has assessable income of $40,000 for YA 2024 and an unabsorbed trade loss of $95,000 for YA 2025. After it carries back what it can to YA 2024, what happens to the remaining $55,000?
Our client keeps its accounts in US dollars and wants to carry back a US$200,000 trade loss for YA 2025 to YA 2024. Which year's exchange rate do we use to turn the S$100,000 limit into US dollars?

Echo Pte Ltd runs a pioneer-status manufacturing trade whose profits are fully tax-exempt, alongside a normally taxed distribution business. The pioneer trade made a loss in YA 2025. Can Echo set that loss against its taxable distribution profits for YA 2024?

After Foxtrot Pte Ltd elects to carry back its YA 2025 loss, its YA 2024 tax falls by $14,000. It still owes $3,000 of property tax on its factory. When should it get the refund, and how much will it receive?

Golf Pte Ltd carried back a $90,000 trade loss for YA 2025 against its YA 2024 income. After a review, IRAS reduces the YA 2025 loss to $60,000. What can IRAS do about each year, and by what date must it act on YA 2024?
Hotel Pte Ltd made a heavy trade loss in YA 2021 and opted for the enhanced carry-back. Against which years' assessable income could that loss be set?

Mr Rahim, a sole proprietor, filed his YA 2025 return without opting to carry back his business loss. IRAS served his notice of assessment on 12 September 2025, and today is 6 October 2025. Can he still elect, and what does he need to send IRAS?

Kestrel Pte Ltd usually files the simplified Form C-S. This year it wants to carry back its YA 2025 loss to YA 2024. Can it still use Form C-S, and how does it give IRAS the recomputed YA 2024 figures?

Mr Lim is one of three partners in a design firm and wants to carry back his share of the firm's YA 2025 loss, but the firm's accounts for 2024 are not yet finalised. Must he file the firm's accounts himself, and what has to be with IRAS before he elects?

Ms Ong, a self-employed physiotherapist and working mother, sets her YA 2025 business loss against her YA 2024 income. What happens to the reliefs she was given for YA 2024 that depend on her earned income?

Ms Chua is a partner in an LLP with a 31 December year end. Her contributed capital was $35,000 at 31 December 2023 and $80,000 at 31 December 2024. She is carrying back her share of the LLP's YA 2025 loss to YA 2024. Which capital figure limits her deduction?

Mr Goh runs a printing business and a cafe as sole proprietor and also earns rent and interest. He is carrying back YA 2025 unabsorbed capital allowances from the printing business to YA 2024. In what order are his YA 2024 income sources used up?

A sole trader's two businesses have YA 2025 unabsorbed capital allowances of $120,000 and $60,000, and his YA 2024 assessable income is $300,000. How is the $100,000 he can carry back split between the two businesses?

Papa Pte Ltd has $30,000 of unabsorbed capital allowances and a $90,000 trade loss for YA 2025, against YA 2024 assessable income of $70,000. If it carries back, which item is used first and how much of each goes back?

In July 2024 the founders of Quill Pte Ltd (31 December year end) sold 70% of its shares to a strategic investor for genuine commercial reasons. Quill wants to carry back its YA 2025 trade loss to YA 2024. Is there a way to do this, and what restriction would apply?

Romeo Pte Ltd has a 31 December year end. On 30 June 2024 a new owner bought 80% of its shares. Romeo wants to carry back both its YA 2025 unabsorbed capital allowances and its YA 2025 trade loss to YA 2024. Does the change in ownership block either of them?
Besides its YA 2025 trade loss, Sierra Pte Ltd has $25,000 of approved donations it could not use in YA 2025. Can it carry those donations back to YA 2024 together with the loss?

For YA 2024, Tango Pte Ltd had income of $120,000 after its own capital allowances. It then deducted $20,000 of its own approved donations and $30,000 of unabsorbed donations transferred from a sister company under group relief. Against what YA 2024 amount can its YA 2025 loss be carried back?
Under s 37D(1B), India Pte Ltd elected to carry back its YA 2020 qualifying deduction over three years. Which year's assessable income must it be set against first, and where does any balance go?
Applying s 37D(14), how many of a shareholder's 10,000 shares count in the 50% comparison if they were issued at $1 each and only 40 cents per share has been paid up?
Under s 37D(8A), by what date must IRAS act if it finds that a YA 2021 qualifying deduction carried back under the three-year scheme against YA 2018 income was excessive?
Does s 37E still let a sole proprietor pass his YA 2025 unabsorbed capital allowances to his wife so they reduce her YA 2024 assessable income?
Can an investment holding company whose income is ascertained under section 10D use section 37D to carry back its unabsorbed capital allowances?

Nimbus Pte Ltd is carrying back its YA 2025 loss against YA 2024 income, part of which was taxed at a 10% concessionary rate. How does s 37D(5) count the amount set against that concessionary income towards the $100,000 limit?
Under Australia's temporary loss carry-back rules, can a company carry back a 2021-22 tax loss against tax it paid for 2018-19 and receive a refundable tax offset?
Under UK corporation tax, how many years back can a company that stops trading carry its terminal trading losses?
If a GST-registered company's input tax exceeds its output tax for a quarter, can it carry the excess back against the GST it paid for the previous quarter?
What rate of stamp duty is payable when a new owner buys 80% of the shares in a private company, changing its shareholders substantially?
Under the Companies Act, what solvency statement must directors make before a company reduces its share capital to write off accumulated losses?
Under the CPF rules, what percentage of his net trade income must a 45-year-old self-employed person pay into MediSave for 2025?

My client's new minimart had its stock on the shelves by 20 March, let walk-in shoppers buy from 28 March, and held a ribbon-cutting launch with a guest of honour on 15 May. Which date does IRAS treat as the start of its business?

A boutique hotel finished its fit-out in May, trained staff in June, applied for registration on 1 July, received its certificate of registration on 12 August and checked in its first guests on 20 August. When did its business commence?

A precision-parts maker installed its machines in November, ran trial batches in January, began commercial output on 3 February and invoiced its first customer on 20 February. Which of these events marks the start of its business for tax purposes?

A company was incorporated to build and sell terrace houses. It paid consultants for site feasibility studies in early 2024, completed its first land purchase in July 2024 and plans to launch sales in 2025. When does its business start for tax purposes?
A developer client capitalises the land price, construction costs, loan interest and property tax on its condominium project. At what point do these costs become deductible?

A proprietary golf club launched its membership sales campaign on 1 November 2024, started building the clubhouse in January 2025, collected its first membership fees in February 2025 and will open its facilities in 2026. Which of these dates does IRAS treat as the start of the club's business?

A distributor with a December financial year end received its first payment in March 2025, but it had been running day-to-day operations since September 2024. Is it bound to treat 1 January 2025 as its start date, or can it argue its business began earlier?

A new company starts a logistics business and a separate software consultancy in the same year, and only the logistics arm enjoys a concessionary rate. Before attributing its pre-opening costs to normal and concessionary income, what must it do first?
A company says some of its pre-opening consultancy fees relate only to its tax-exempt income. What must it put in its tax computation to back up that claim?
Does a start-up need to attach the lease and invoices supporting its pre-revenue expense claims when it files its first corporate tax return?

A newly licensed bank needs to apportion shared pre-opening costs between its normal-rate and concessionary income in its first YA. What apportionment bases does IRAS accept, and is there one specific to banks?

A company incorporated in 2013 paid patent filing costs in 2014 and 2015, started trading on 1 January 2016, and was awarded a 10% incentive that took effect from 1 July 2016. Under the treatment that applied to those costs, against which income are they deducted?

In its first YA, a company's normal-rate income is too small to absorb the pre-commencement expenses allocated to it, but it also earns income taxed at 10% under an incentive. Can the shortfall be set off against the incentive income, and is any adjustment required?

Before its first sale, a start-up paid petrol, parking and insurance for the director's S-plated private car used on business errands. Can those costs be claimed as pre-revenue expenses once it starts earning?

Eight months before earning its first revenue, a start-up incurred costs that would have attracted a further deduction had it already been trading. Once revenue starts, can it claim the further deduction as well, or only the basic deduction?
The sole shareholder-director of a newly incorporated SME puts his wife on the payroll as an administrator at $9,000 a month. Can the company deduct her full salary?

A company with pioneer status has its qualifying profits exempted under the Economic Expansion Incentives Act. When attributing its pre-opening expenses to income streams in its first year, does that pioneer income count as exempt income?
Under s 14R(2)(c), a company with a 31 March year end paid office rent in September 2024 and earned its first fee in May 2025. On what date is that rent treated as incurred?
A start-up relies on s 14R to claim a pre-revenue expense under another deduction provision in Part 5. Does s 14R(3) excuse it from that provision's own qualifying conditions?
Under s 14X(3), how does the Comptroller decide whether rent a company paid before it started trading should be set against its concessionary income, given that it had no income at the time?

Section 14(1) only allows expenses incurred in producing income, so the start date of a business matters. Does the Income Tax Act itself define when a business actually commences, or is that a question of fact?

Section 14R only works for what it calls an applicable basis period. A company earned its first business receipt in its YA 2011 basis period. Could it deduct revenue expenses from the 12 months before that basis period began?
Under s 14X(2), are qualifying innovation project costs a company incurred before it began trading caught by the attribution rule, and on what date are they treated as incurred?
A start-up registered for GST three months after it began trading. Can it claim input tax on the equipment it bought before its GST registration date, and what conditions apply?
How much stamp duty is payable on the three-year tenancy agreement a new supermarket signs for its shop unit?
Under Malaysian income tax law, can a newly incorporated Sdn Bhd deduct the expenses it incurred before its first sale?
Under the Companies Act, by when must a newly incorporated private company hold its first annual general meeting?
What fee does a new hotel pay the Hotels Licensing Board for its certificate of registration, and how often must it be renewed?
By what day of the following month must a newly registered employer pay the CPF contributions for its staff's wages?
How does s 14N(8A) apply the $300,000 renovation cap when a four-partner accounting firm refits its office? Does each partner get a separate cap?

Lim Trading (31 December year end) first claimed renovation deductions in YA 2023, so its old three-year window runs to YA 2025. It claimed on $120,000 of works for YA 2023 and $100,000 for YA 2024, and spends $280,000 on a refit in calendar 2024. How much of the $280,000 qualifies?

A company incorporated in mid-2025 starts trading at once and closes its first accounts on 31 December 2025, so its first year of assessment is YA 2026. Is its renovation expenditure cap for the current fixed block cut down because it was not trading in all three years?

During its office refit, Tan Logistics bought new split air-conditioning units and is claiming capital allowances on them as plant. Can it also include the same air-con cost in its renovation deduction claim?
For YA 2025 a company's renovation deduction is larger than its trade income, leaving an unused balance. Can that balance be set against the company's assessable income of YA 2024?

In 2026 IRAS finds that a client's shop renovation, on which it claimed deductions in each of YA 2023, YA 2024 and YA 2025, included removing a structural column that needed Building Control approval the client never obtained. How will IRAS claw back those deductions?

A fashion retailer fitting out a new mall unit is paying for changing cubicles, temporary hoarding around the site and insurance cover for the works. Do these items qualify for the renovation deduction?
A company spent $90,000 renovating its showroom in FY2023 but left the deduction out of its YA 2024 return. Can it claim the whole amount in its YA 2025 return instead?

A property investment holding company is taxed on its rental income under the special regime for companies whose business is making investments. It has just refurbished two apartments it leases out. Can it claim the renovation deduction?
A small company files Form C-S and does not have to send in a tax computation. How does it take up the option to write off its FY2024 renovation costs in a single year?

Under the former section 14DA, an executive director who leads a company's in-house R&D in Singapore is paid a salary plus director's fees. Which part of her pay counts as staff costs for the enhanced R&D deduction?

Under the former section 14KA, an approved Singapore company posts two engineers to its new Vietnam subsidiary in 2025 and pays them base salary, a housing allowance and a year-end bonus. Which of these payments can get the further deduction?

Under the former section 14WA, a company licenses a patented process from an unrelated overseas firm in FY2024 and also pays lawyers to negotiate the licence agreement. Do the legal fees qualify for the enhanced licensing deduction?
The controlling shareholder of a trading company puts his wife on the payroll at $15,000 a month for a few hours of admin work each week. Can the company deduct her full salary?
A company's only rental property, a shophouse it lets out, stood empty for five months in 2025 between tenants. Can it deduct the property tax and maintenance costs it paid while the unit was empty?

A company should have registered for GST in 2024 but only registered in 2025 after IRAS caught up with it, and it had to pay out of its own pocket the GST it ought to have charged on its 2024 sales. Can it deduct that GST against its income, or is some other income tax relief available?

Under s 14ZE, a company signs a three-year shop lease with an option to renew for another three years, and pays the agent's commission and stamp duty. Does the renewal option take the lease outside the deduction?
A trading company buys a new five-seater saloon car, registered in Singapore in 2025, for its sales director to visit clients. Can it claim capital allowances on the car?
In FY2025 a design studio buys 12 height-adjustable office desks at $4,000 each. Can it write off all $48,000 in YA 2026 as low-value assets?

A manufacturer bought a machine for $200,000 and has claimed initial and annual allowances on it totalling $200,000. It now sells the machine for $260,000. On what amount is the balancing charge made?

A logistics company sells an old forklift, which would trigger a $25,000 balancing charge, and buys a replacement forklift for $70,000. Can it avoid the balancing charge, and how are allowances on the new forklift affected?

To install a heavy industrial oven, a bakery had to strengthen the floor slab and widen the doorway of its rented unit. Can those building works be added to the oven's cost for capital allowance purposes?
A private limited company is converting into a limited liability partnership. Can its machinery pass to the LLP at its tax written-down value so that no balancing charge arises on the conversion?

Under s 22A, a company has $50,000 of unused capital allowances left over from YA 2023 and $80,000 of allowances for YA 2025 itself, but its YA 2025 profit is only $60,000. Which allowances are used first?
My client is signing a three-year office lease at $12,000 a month. How much stamp duty is payable on the lease, and within how many days must it be stamped?
How long does the Commissioner of Building Control usually take to approve plans for removing a load-bearing wall in a shop unit, and what submission fee is charged?
A Singapore company's Malaysian subsidiary renovated its Johor Bahru office. Under Malaysian income tax law, can the subsidiary deduct the renovation cost, and is there a cap?
What Skills Development Levy rate must a company pay on each employee's monthly wages, and what are the minimum and maximum amounts per employee?
Over how many years should a company depreciate its office fit-out in its statutory financial statements under SFRS(I) 1-16?
Under the Employment Act, how many days of paid annual leave must a company give a clerk who has worked for it for five years?

Our client is incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, but all its directors live in Singapore and every board meeting where strategy and key decisions are made is held here. Is it a Singapore tax resident company?

A Singapore company earns interest on a fixed deposit it keeps with a bank in Dubai and never transfers the money home. Instead it uses the interest to pay down a loan it took out for its Singapore business. Is the interest treated as having been remitted to Singapore?

A Singapore subsidiary of a Japanese group held a warehouse in Thailand for its own logistics operations. Title passed to the buyer on 15 December 2023 and the gain was brought into Singapore in March 2024. Is the gain caught by the rule that taxes remitted gains from selling overseas assets?
HoldCo Pte Ltd received a $300,000 dividend in 2025 from its wholly owned Singapore-resident subsidiary. Does HoldCo have to pay income tax on it?

A Singapore-resident company brings home a dividend from its subsidiary in a country whose top corporate income tax rate is 12%, where the underlying profits were taxed. Can the dividend qualify for the foreign-sourced income exemption?
Alpha Pte Ltd, incorporated in 2012, has chargeable income of $150,000 for YA 2025. How much of that income is exempt under the partial tax exemption for companies?

NewCo Pte Ltd was incorporated in Singapore in 2025 and is 100% owned by its Singapore parent company, with no individual shareholders. Can NewCo claim the tax exemption for new start-up companies in its first year of assessment?

A Singapore company pays an annual royalty to a German company, which has no branch or other permanent establishment here, for the right to use a patented manufacturing process. Is the royalty taxable in Singapore, and at what rate, applied to the full payment, before any treaty relief?

A Singapore subsidiary of a US group keeps its statutory accounts in US dollars because that is its functional currency. Which exchange rate should it use to convert its chargeable income into Singapore dollars for the tax computation?
Beta Pte Ltd closes its books on 30 June. For the financial year ended 30 June 2025, by what date must it lodge its estimated chargeable income if IRAS grants no extension?
IRAS served a company's notice of assessment for YA 2025 on 10 November 2025, and the company disagrees with a disallowed deduction. What is the last day for it to lodge an objection?

A company that should have registered for GST in 2022 only registered in 2024, and had to pay IRAS the output tax on its earlier sales out of its own pocket. Those sales, including the GST element, were taxed as income for YA 2023. Can its YA 2023 income tax assessment be revised to give relief?
After the company's objection failed, IRAS issued a notice of refusal to amend dated 2 March 2026. What must the company lodge with the Board of Review to appeal, and by when?
Our firm's senior tax manager prepared a client company's appeal. She is neither a lawyer nor a public accountant. Can she represent the company at the Board of Review hearing?
A client has lodged an objection to its YA 2025 assessment. Can it hold back payment of the disputed tax until IRAS decides on the objection?

In both 2023 and 2024, the only person on my client's payroll was its sole shareholder, who also serves as its director, and the company paid CPF for her. Does it qualify for the $2,000 cash grant given with the YA 2024 and YA 2025 corporate income tax rebates?

In March 2026 a company finds that its YA 2022 tax return, which IRAS assessed in 2022, left out a deductible expense. Can it still ask IRAS for relief because of the mistake, and what is the deadline?
Because of careless bookkeeping, a company's Form C left out $120,000 of sales, so its tax was undercharged by $20,400. If the company is convicted, what penalty can it be ordered to pay?
In 2026 IRAS finds that a company's directors wilfully hid sales from its YA 2019 return. The usual time limit has passed; can IRAS still raise an additional assessment under section 74?
Under section 87, a company's $50,000 tax bill fell due on 15 January 2026 and is still unpaid. What late-payment penalties apply, and is there a ceiling?
A company keeps a second, falsified set of books to understate its profits and cut its tax. If it is convicted under section 96A, what penalty does it face?

A property developer decides in March 2025 to keep three unsold apartments from its development stock and lease them out long term as investments. Under the former section 10P, what amount is brought in as its income, and for which basis period?

My client, a Singapore manufacturing company, has held a 22% ordinary shareholding in an unlisted Singapore logistics company since mid-2022 and plans to sell the whole stake in March 2026. Will the gain be exempt under the former section 13Z?

A client approved for the IP Development Incentive elected one of its patents for the concessionary rate in its YA 2024 return. Under the former section 43ZI, can it leave that patent out of the election for YA 2025?
Under the Companies Act, what late lodgement penalty does ACRA charge a private company that files its annual return after the deadline?
My client's Malaysian subsidiary is an SME with chargeable income of RM500,000. What rate of Malaysian income tax applies to its first RM150,000?
What penalty does IRAS impose under the GST Act when a GST-registered company files its quarterly GST return late?
What rate of stamp duty is payable when a company buys shares in an unlisted Singapore private company?
Under the CPF Act, what rate of late-payment interest does the CPF Board charge an employer that pays its employees' monthly CPF contributions late?
What profits tax rate applies to the first HK$2 million of a Hong Kong corporation's assessable profits under the two-tiered system?
